task.description:
docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml (status: open) reports that `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` currently fails on main with three type warnings in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, all shaped 'a struct for Letflow.Engine.InstanceState is expected on struct update ... but got type: dynamic(...) ... you must also pattern match on %Letflow.Engine.InstanceState{}', at dispatch_start/4 (line ~220), dispatch_end/3 (line ~235), and dispatch_human_task/3 (line ~246). Verified directly against origin/main in an isolated worktree by ORCH before filing -- this is a real, currently-standing break in the compile gate every future WF-02/WF-03 run's Step 2a/Step 3 relies on, not a transient local artifact.

Step 0.5: check docs/issues/ for a resolved entry with matching symptoms first -- ISS-0044 covers different warnings (mix test deprecations/unused-args/migration-reload), not this compile-time struct-update class, so this is likely NOT a recurrence, but confirm rather than assume.

Step 1: reproduce directly (mix compile --warnings-as-errors on a clean _build), then trace to root cause rather than trusting ISS-0046's own hypothesis. ISS-0046's filed hypothesis: dispatch_node/4 (transition.ex ~154-197) dispatches on node.node_type across six clauses, and none of them -- including the catch-all at ~190-196, which matches only %Node{node_type: node_type, id: node_id} and leaves instance_state/token as untyped wildcards -- ever pattern-matches instance_state against %InstanceState{}, so Elixir 1.20's set-theoretic type checker cannot narrow instance_state's type through that dispatch, and the three affected private functions' %InstanceState{instance_state | ...} struct-update syntax degrades to a warning. Confirm or correct this independently -- do not just restate it.

Do NOT implement the fix in this step. Read lib/letflow/design/req044-transition-kernel.md first to understand this module's established idiom (design doc for the module you're diagnosing) so your diagnosis names a fix shape consistent with it, not just 'add a pattern match somewhere'.
acceptance_criteria: mix compile --warnings-as-errors reproduced directly on this branch (not assumed from the issue's own text), actual output quoted
root cause traced to the specific line/clause responsible, confirmed or corrected against ISS-0046's own hypothesis, not just restated
diagnosis names which function(s) need a fix and the shape of the fix (e.g. an explicit %InstanceState{} = instance_state pattern where), without writing the actual fix
explicitly states whether this is a recurrence of any resolved issue (checked docs/issues/*.yaml, esp. ISS-0044) or a new defect class

result.summary:
Step 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for status: resolved entries. ISS-0044 (WF03-ISS0044-20260818) is the only prior entry touching mix compile/test warnings, but its symptoms are mix test-time deprecation/unused-arg/migration-reload warnings in a different module class -- confirmed NOT a match, this is a new defect class (compile-time struct-update type-inference gap under --warnings-as-errors). No recurrence.

Step 1 (diagnose): reproduced directly. `rm -rf _build/dev/lib/letflow && mix compile --warnings-as-errors` on this branch (Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29, local toolchain, not Docker) fails with exactly 3 warnings, all in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, matching ISS-0046's count but CORRECTING its per-warning attribution: (1) line 218, dispatch_start/4 -- struct update `%Token{token | node_id: edge.target}` warns that `token` has inferred type dynamic(), 'must also pattern match on %Letflow.Engine.Token{}'. ISS-0046 mischaracterized this as an InstanceState warning at line ~220; it is actually a Token warning at line 218, one line earlier, and the struct in question is Token, not InstanceState. (2) line 235, dispatch_end/3 -- `%InstanceState{instance_state | tokens: remaining_tokens, status: new_status}` warns instance_state has type dynamic(%{..., tokens: term()}). (3) line 246, dispatch_human_task/3 -- `%InstanceState{instance_state | pending_task_nodes: new_pending}` warns instance_state has type dynamic(%{..., pending_task_nodes: list(term())}).

Root cause, corrected against ISS-0046's own hypothesis: ISS-0046 attributed the gap to dispatch_node/4's catch-all clause never pattern-matching instance_state/token against their structs. That is not the actual mechanism -- read dispatch_node/4 (transition.ex:151-197) directly: every one of its 6 clauses (including the catch-all) receives instance_state and token as bare variables, true, but the REAL narrowing loss happens one level down. transition/3 itself (line 144) DOES pattern-match `%InstanceState{} = instance_state` in its own head, so instance_state IS a narrowed %InstanceState{} at the point it is passed into dispatch_node/4. The type narrowing is lost when it crosses into dispatch_start/4, dispatch_end/3, and dispatch_human_task/3 -- three PRIVATE functions that take instance_state/token as bare, unpattern-matched parameters and have NO @spec of their own (unlike dispatch_node/4, dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4, find_node/2, replace_token/2, which all declare one). Elixir 1.20's set-theoretic type checker does not propagate a caller's already-narrowed struct type through an unspec'd function boundary into that function's own parameter bindings -- each function's parameter types are (re)inferred from that function's own head/body, not inherited from the call site. Empirically confirmed in isolation (scratch .ex files, cleaned up after): a private function with a @spec declaring a struct-typed parameter but no pattern match in its head still produces the exact same struct-update warning (@spec alone does not narrow); adding an explicit `%TestStruct{} = s` pattern match to the SAME function's parameter, with or without a @spec, produces a clean compile. So the @spec presence/absence on dispatch_node/4 is a red herring -- what actually matters is that dispatch_start/4, dispatch_end/3, and dispatch_human_task/3 never pattern-match their own instance_state/token parameters against %InstanceState{}/%Token{} in their own heads.

Why existing tests didn't catch it: this is a compile-time --warnings-as-errors gate failure, not a runtime defect -- test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs's assertions run fine under plain `mix test` (warnings don't fail assertions), so nothing in the test suite itself exercises the warnings-as-errors compile gate; only a dedicated `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` run (or CI step) surfaces it.

Fix shape for CODE-DESIGNER (do not implement here): add an explicit struct pattern match to each of the three affected private functions' own parameter list, matching this module's already-established idiom elsewhere in the same file (dispatch_node/4's clauses already do exactly this for their `node`/4th parameter, e.g. `%Node{node_type: :START} = node`) -- i.e. `defp dispatch_start(definition_snapshot, instance_state, %Token{} = token, node)` (the warning here is on token, not instance_state) and `defp dispatch_end(%InstanceState{} = instance_state, token, _node)` and `defp dispatch_human_task(%InstanceState{} = instance_state, token, _node)`. This is a minimal, mechanical, in-idiom fix -- no restructuring of dispatch_node/4's own dispatch shape is needed, since the loss happens one call-level below it, not at its own catch-all clause as ISS-0046 guessed.
